_README: Per-nationality visa deep-dive: Nepal → Korea. Grounded in official channels (Korea Visa Portal visa.go.kr; Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Nepal, overseas.mofa.go.kr/np-en; appointment portal koreanembassynepal.org). Fee/processing are VOLATILE (factId visa-nepal-c39). No invented figures. Single consular jurisdiction (Kathmandu), so no jurisdiction block.
metaTitle: Nepal to Korea Visa: Do You Need One? (2026) — Korea Trip Hub
metaDesc: Yes — Nepali passport holders need a visa for South Korea (C-3-9 short-term tourist, up to 90 days). Book an online appointment at the Korean Embassy in Kathmandu: documents, fee (NPR 5,400) and processing time.

verdict.headline: Yes — Nepali passport holders need a visa.
verdict.sub: You'll apply for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa (single entry, stay up to 90 days) at the Korean Embassy in Kathmandu, by online appointment. K-ETA/visa-free entry does NOT apply to Nepali passports.
verdict.entry: Single entry (multiple-entry possible in some cases — ask at the embassy)

tldr: Fill the form at visa.go.kr (the ONLY official portal), then print and sign it.
Book an online appointment at koreanembassynepal.org — slots open Mondays and Wednesdays at 10:00.
Have Nepali documents translated into English AND notarized; Korean documents must be originals issued within the last 3 months.
Fee NPR 5,400 (single entry), cash at the counter; result in about 21 working days.

items.title: Confirm the visa type
items.detail: For tourism you want the C-3-9 short-term visit (tourist) visa. Gather the checklist below before you start.

items.title: Fill the form at visa.go.kr
items.detail: Go to the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr) — the only official site. Complete the application form, print and sign it. One form per applicant.

items.title: Book an online appointment
items.detail: Reserve a slot at koreanembassynepal.org. Appointment slots open on Mondays and Wednesdays at 10:00 — book early, they fill fast.

items.title: Assemble & prepare your documents
items.detail: Collect the checklist below. Nepali documents must be translated into English and notarized; any Korean documents must be originals issued within the last 3 months.

items.title: Attend the appointment & pay
items.detail: Submit your form and documents in person at the Korean Embassy in Kathmandu at your appointment time, and pay the NPR 5,400 fee in cash at the counter.

items.title: Wait for processing
items.detail: Processing takes about 21 working days. Don't book non-refundable flights until you're approved; you may be asked for more documents.

items.title: Collect your passport
items.detail: Pick it up as instructed and check the visa sticker details (name, dates, entry type) the moment you receive it.

documents.title: Document checklist — with where & how to get each
documents.intro: This is the part every other site skips. For each document, here is exactly where you obtain it and what it must show. Nepali documents need an English translation and notarization.

rows.how: Valid 6+ months beyond your trip, with at least 2 blank pages. Bring old passports too if you have them.
Complete on the Korea Visa Portal, print and sign. One per applicant.
One recent passport-size photo, plain white background, taken within the last 6 months, full face.
A confirmed reservation with departure at least 21 days after you apply. Do NOT buy a paid ticket before approval, and never submit a fake ticket.
Confirmed hotel bookings covering your stay. Staying with someone? Add an invitation letter + host's ID/ARC copy.
A letter stating the purpose of your visit and a day-by-day plan.
A recent statement (with the bank's seal) showing you can fund the trip. Nepali documents need English translation + notarization.
Employed: employment/leave letter. Self-employed: business registration. Student: enrolment certificate. Translated to English and notarized.

funds.title: "How much bank balance do I need?"
funds.body: There is no single official minimum published for the tourist visa. What matters is proving you can comfortably fund the whole trip and have reasons to return to Nepal. Case officers look at stability, not just a headline number.
tips: Show a consistent balance — a large deposit made days before applying looks weak.
Pair the bank statement with proof of your job, business or studies; together they tell a credible story.
Being sponsored? Add the sponsor's bank statement, a signed sponsorship letter, and proof of your relationship.

items.d: Submitting a fake ticket or false travel details can bring a rejection AND a 3-year ban on re-applying. Use a genuine reservation.
Nepali documents must be translated into English and notarized. Un-translated or un-notarized papers get sent back.
Appointment slots open Mondays and Wednesdays at 10:00 and fill quickly. Plan your booking around them.
Paying for non-refundable tickets before approval. A reservation (departure 21+ days out) is enough for the file.
Wrong size, colored background, glasses or an old photo. Use a fresh white-background passport photo.

items.q: Do Nepali citizens need a visa for Korea?
items.a: Yes — for tourism you apply in advance for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa. Nepali passports are not visa-free and not on the K-ETA list.

items.q: How do I get an appointment?
items.a: Book online at koreanembassynepal.org. Slots open on Mondays and Wednesdays at 10:00 and fill fast, so book as early as you can.
About 21 working days, and longer during peak season or if extra checks are needed. Apply well ahead of your trip.
NPR 5,400 for a single-entry short-term visa, paid in cash at the embassy counter. Amounts change — confirm the current fee at the embassy.
Yes — Nepali documents must be translated into English and notarized. Any Korean documents must be originals issued within the last 3 months.

items.q: Why does the flight need to depart 21+ days after applying?
items.a: The embassy expects your travel dates to allow for processing (about 21 working days). Book a reservation with a departure at least 21 days out — and never a fake ticket.

items.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
items.a: Multiple-entry tourist visas are possible in some cases, but eligibility varies. Ask at the embassy about current rules for Nepal.

items.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?
items.a: The e-Arrival Card requirement can still apply on entry. Check the entry-document rules close to your travel date on the official sites.
